regime.summary: Easing cycle (last MPC cut 50bp to 10.5%) with CPI flat at 5.6%, so real rates stay high. But the 6M bill at 10.16% sits near the policy rate, so little further easing is priced. KSE100 is up 58.9% in 12m, so the market is extended. Mutual funds are buying while foreigners and banks sell. Stay partly invested in cash-rich, catalyst-led sectors; add no chase positions.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 10.5%; last MPC decision 2025-12-15: cut (-50bp)
CPI YoY 5.6% for 2025-12 (published by 2026-01-03); three months earlier (2025-09) 5.6%
6M T-bill minus policy rate -0.34pp (market near policy rate)
Lesson: favour sectors with their own catalyst over rate-sensitive ones.

core.thesis: Fertilizer leader trading at 5.5x earnings with an 11.2% dividend yield, next to its 252-day high. The sector has strong 6m momentum. In the 2024 first-cut regime fertilizer led while banks lagged, so own catalyst beats rate sensitivity. Risk: eps_yoy is slightly negative and the stock is extended.

evidence.quote: fertilizer, E&P and pharma led while banks lagged

core.thesis: E&P major at 5.6x earnings with a 6.8% dividend yield, near its high. Mutual funds are net buyers of E&P in both the 5 and 20 session windows, and sector 3m return is 20%. A falling oil price (Brent -3.2% over 3m) is the main risk, so keep it a small weight.
